feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 1 (72 mm span, 16 mm footprints, lead 0.03 m, track 0.10 m) still had line_loss_events of 1 per run and max_error of about 0.061 m on the oval and s-bend. The score fell from 79.6 to 56.2 mainly because s-bend progress dropped from 0.29 to 0.18. That suggests the lead or track change hurt more than the wider span helped. I had to compensate for the wider span by keeping the controller fixed and using weights proportional to sensor x, scaled to about 1 per 30 mm. The seven-sensor array raises the risk of steering_oscillation because it changes the signal more often at edge crossings. Interpret the next race as follows. If line_loss_events fall to 0 and max_error stays near 0.061 m, the reach is not the sole cause. Then move to turn authority, for example wheel_track 0.08 m. If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more, the reach at the outer edge is still too short. In that case try x = ±0.072 m with 16 mm footprints. If progress on the s-bend stays below 0.25 while line loss is zero, restore the lead to y = 0.05 m, because the shorter lead may be reacting too late.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events are 0 but max_error still reaches about 0.06 m on the oval or s-bend, try wheel_track 0.08 m with mass 0.8 kg, since turn authority would then be the limit, not sensing.

If line_loss_events stay at 1 or more on the s-bend or slalom, widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.072 m with 7 sensors at 24 mm spacing and 16 mm footprints, because iteration 1 showed loss at about 0.0565 m offset.

If the s-bend progress stays below 0.25 with line loss at 0, restore the lead to y = 0.05 m, since iteration 0 (lead 0.05 m, track 0.12 m) reached progress 0.29 on the s-bend and iteration 1's shorter lead coincided with a drop to 0.18.
